observations: Torah #198 has zero bechina edges in torahData.js, and the source text contains no bechina language. The teaching presents exactly one relationship: a person who cries out (צועק) to God is told to travel/move forward (ליסע), proven from Exodus 14:15. This is a pure eitza relationship — cause-and-effect, directional — not a bechina equivalence. The framework requires bechina-connected concepts (sharing the same essential nature) to form a package. Since there are no bechina relationships in this Torah at all, and the two core concepts (צְעָקָה and נְסִיעָה) are causally related rather than essentially equivalent, no package can be proposed — not even with minimum size of two nodes. Adding the eitza edge צְעָקָה → נְסִיעָה to the dataset would be the correct enrichment action, but it would yield zero packages. There is no candidate cluster of concepts sharing a common essence in this teaching.
